🔧 Language models

Fine-tuning

In simple words

Extra training that takes a model that has already learned a lot and adjusts it for a particular job.

Extra training for a model that has already learned from lots of general data, using a smaller set of examples for one particular task or style. Chatbots are built this way: first pre-training on huge amounts of text, then fine-tuning to follow instructions and give helpful answers.

Example. A great all-round athlete who starts training for one sport doesn't learn to run from scratch, but sharpens the skills for that sport. A general language model can be fine-tuned in the same way to answer like a helpful assistant.

Related words

  • TrainingThe process in which a model learns from examples by making guesses and correcting its mistakes again and again.
  • Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)A way to make a chatbot more helpful: people rate its answers, and those ratings become its reward in reinforcement learning.
